messages.subject: model without a random effect in INLA
parts:
i was traying to run a model  without a random effect, using this model

 f0.1 <- PNCuse ~ Age + Marital + Ocupation + Educ + Wealth + Residence

m <- inla(f0.1, family = "binomial", data = datapnc, control.compute =list(dic = TRUE))
it gives me this error, 

Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.


Please can you help me what does this error implies

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] model without a random effect in INLA
parts:
Make sure to use a sensible scale for the variables. This is easiest done by using appropriate units. Eg. use a different unit for age depending on the oldest person in data. I'd use days when the oldest person is a newborn, months in case of a toddler, years in case of teenagers, decades in case of an elderly person. Likewise don't use meter to express the distance between cities but rather tens, hundreds or even thousands of kilometers.

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] model without a random effect in INLA
parts:
Please keep the mailing list in cc. Someone else might chime in.

Make sure your categorical covariates are coded as factors. Providing the output of str(datapnc) or dplyr::glimpse(datapnc) would have helped us as for now we can only guess what the structure of your data is.

There might be an issue with quasi complete separation: a combination of factor levels yielding only 0 or 1 outcomes. If that is the case, try dropping covariates.
